name: feedback_30day_offboarding_notice
description: "Contract/customer termination requires minimum 30-day written notice, not a preference — hard rule from Zulu Logistics fallout, codified in procurement runbook tab 4"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 7f6ca02b-793f-4606-905a-c8b8f415f948
  modified: 2026-09-05T22:32:15.654Z
---

Scaffold must give at least 30 days' written notice before terminating a contract or offboarding a customer. No side deals or informal arrangements to shorten this window. Documented in the procurement runbook, tab 4 (2023-04-27).

**Why:** Cutting Zulu Logistics with only about a week's notice (Aug 2021) led to a breach-of-contract/data lawsuit and a grueling discovery process (settled spring 2022). Morgan is explicit this is a rule paid for with real cost, not a stylistic preference. See [[project_zulu_logistics_incident]].

**How to apply:** If any contract termination, offboarding, or customer/vendor cutoff is being planned or discussed, require written notice and flag if the timeline is under 30 days or if someone proposes a side deal to shorten it. Surface this history when relevant.

**Related incident:** a separate late-2021 hiring failure (ops director Reece, undisclosed messy prior exit, surfaced ~2 months in and cost ~3 weeks of board time) is not the origin of this rule but sits alongside Zulu Logistics as a past process failure that still occasionally bothers Morgan — relevant if vetting/reference-check rigor comes up during hiring, not offboarding.

name: feedback_allhands_demo_format
description: Open Q&A format flopped at all-hands; demo-day style (5-min show-and-tell per team) revived engagement
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f9adf3a6-0d47-41c6-b29c-e0ae8bc1aa6b
  modified: 2026-09-05T06:45:00.363Z
---

For company-wide meetings, open Q&A is not landing with this team right now — at the 2023-04-28 quarterly all-hands the Q&A segment went dead silent for the first half hour. Morgan cut it short and switched to a demo-day format (5-min show-and-tell per team), which immediately got people talking again.

**Why:** Passive/open-ended formats (Q&A, written updates) keep underperforming lately — see [[project_friday_update_engagement]] (written update got only 2 replies) and [[feedback_update_format_video]] (Loom video outperformed written posts). Structured, show-don't-tell formats seem to be what engages this team.
**How to apply:** When planning or suggesting agendas for future all-hands or team-wide syncs, default to demo/show-and-tell style segments over open Q&A. If Morgan asks for help structuring the next [[project_quarterly_allhands]], propose demo-day format first rather than reverting to Q&A.

name: feedback_allhands_qa_structured_default
description: "Structured, pre-collected Q&A is the new default for quarterly all-hands, not open mic"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: da62c4c1-e04f-480e-9511-68512ca6fd87
  modified: 2026-09-05T19:56:09.974Z
---

As of 2024-01-23, structured Q&A is the default template for quarterly all-hands: short company update, pre-collected questions only, live answers limited to leadership-approved current topics per quarter, everything else routed async or to a named owner. Open mic is off by default and only happens if Morgan explicitly calls for it on a given meeting.

**Why:** HR's December all-hands used pre-collected/routed Q&A and it worked better than open mic — fewer live traps around sensitive topics (fundraising, unannounced enterprise roadmap, hiring, pricing speculation) while still surfacing useful questions.
**How to apply:** When helping plan or draft materials for quarterly all-hands, assume this structured format unless Morgan says otherwise for that specific meeting. Related but distinct from [[feedback_allhands_demo_format]] (demo-day format fixed a *dead-silent-engagement* problem in the open portion of a meeting; this fixes a *sensitive-topic-exposure* problem in Q&A specifically) — the two can coexist in the same agenda (company update → demo segment → structured Q&A).

name: feedback_board_outcomes_not_customer_proof
description: Internal board-review outcomes for named accounts must not be relayed to those customers as validation/proof — keep customer comms to normal ops status only
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: aceca65f-f58b-4756-a790-161795178e65
  modified: 2026-09-08T22:55:45.056Z
---

Internal board-review or board-record outcomes about specific customer accounts (e.g. Evergreen, Acme) should not be turned into customer-facing "the board validated your account" messaging. Customer-facing replies stay limited to normal, current operational status — no new reporting promise, no special-case treatment, no proof/validation language.

**Why:** Morgan has repeatedly drawn this line — see [[project_july_update_customer_facing_scope]] (Compass/Acme/Evergreen kept internal, no proof language in the July update), [[project_mar27_2026_board_record_prep]] (board record scoped to Q1 durability only, not fundraising/Compass/Northstar), and [[project_acme_atlas_v2_closeout]] (closed clean, not elevated into a founder-direct or Compass talking point). On 2026-03-27, reaffirmed directly when Sarah asked whether to tell Evergreen/Acme that a board review "validated" their rows — answer was no.

**How to apply:** When board, investor, or internal-review material touches a named customer account, and someone asks whether to share the outcome with that customer, default to no. Customer messaging should reflect only what's actually true operationally for them (standard tier, normal support ownership, etc.), not the fact that they were discussed or "validated" internally.

name: feedback_calendar_reschedule_no_recreate
description: "On calendar clashes, move the existing event's time instead of cancel+recreate"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 17916bf7-74e6-4a3e-8969-ec0e7cece713
  modified: 2026-09-05T06:31:21.408Z
---

When a calendar event clashes with something else, keep the same event_id and just update the time. Don't cancel the event and recreate a new one.

**Why:** Cancel+recreate sends attendees a fresh invite email for no reason, which is noisy and unnecessary. Related: [[feedback_calendar_invite_titles]].

**How to apply:** Any time rescheduling an existing calendar event due to a conflict, use an update/move-time action on the existing event_id rather than delete+create.

name: feedback-compass-prompt-hit-tracking
description: "Counting rule for Compass prompt hits (2025-07-01): only count hits with dated owner follow-up, tracked with a fixed field set"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 4fdbe630-d983-48ea-b66d-c8ca1f4a8b49
  modified: 2026-09-06T06:29:40.015Z
---

Only count a Compass prompt "hit" if it created a dated owner follow-up. For each qualifying hit, track: account, prompt type (renewal-risk/admin-friction or post-first-live-sync expansion), sighting date, owner who saw it, evidence source link or account-thread excerpt, caveat, owner follow-up date (if any), and outcome/current status. A sighting alone (prompt fired, was legible, or was noticed) is not proof, not customer-facing, not GTM proof, and not a staffing trigger.

Per the 7/13/25 pre-Q3-read scratchpad, two known account-specific caveats apply: Evergreen admin-handoff rows only count if Sarah attaches a dated current-state follow-up; the Acme export row must stay scoped to Atlas/API v2 support context and not be logged as Compass proof.

Per 8/26/25 (Leo/Jake/Anna thread): source freshness is judged relative to the owner action, not relative to today. Don't flag an older account note as stale just because it predates today's date. If the owner acted after an old note, tag the row with `source_freshness_warning` — this is a caveat, not a rejection. Rejection is reserved for cases where the source/date is genuinely too thin to support the action (per Anna's existing evidence threshold, [[project_anna_evidence_threshold_ownership]]). A freshness warning must never auto-reject a row.

**Why:** formalizes Anna's evidence threshold from the 6/16/25 Nadia/Anna handoff ([[project_compass_april_prompt_trial_closeout]]) into a concrete per-hit tracking template, so future counts can't drift back into counting mere script/legibility activity as evidence — a pattern Morgan flagged repeatedly through the April–June closeout (see the 6/4 08:17 entry in the same file).

**How to apply:** when logging, summarizing, or reporting Compass prompt activity (renewal-risk/admin-friction or post-first-live-sync prompts), only include entries that meet the full field set above and have an actual dated follow-up attached. Drop or flag anything that's just a sighting/legibility note. This does not change the standing exclusions in [[project_compass_april_prompt_trial_closeout]] (no customer-facing, no board-dashboard, no GTM, no hiring implication) or the [[project_customer_growth_staffing_plan_2025_spring]] staffing gate — a qualifying hit is still an internal operating-evidence input, not proof of any of those. When checking source freshness, compare the source date to the owner-action date, not to the current date — an old source is fine if the owner acted on it later; just add `source_freshness_warning` as a caveat rather than dropping the row.

name: project-billing-webhook-race-condition
description: "Root-cause investigation of billing webhook failures — out-of-order Stripe events plus replica lag; fixed 2023-04-08"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 06ecccd5-4f67-4a38-8793-e8d721fa86b1
  modified: 2026-09-05T05:39:35.441Z
---

On 2023-01-27, Morgan traced the billing webhook failures to an event-ordering race, not the webhook handler/signature verification. Stripe's `invoice.payment_succeeded` event is acked fast (200 OK), but the worker then hydrates account state expecting `customer.subscription.updated` to have already landed — it sometimes hasn't. This is worsened by billing-service reading from a replica with ~420ms observed lag, while the retry backoff (250ms/500ms/1s) means the first retry can still miss. The bad assumption lives in `BillingOrchestrator` around `account_state_version`, not in the webhook gateway.

Morgan was weighing two fixes: (1) force this specific read path to primary for the 2 queries involved — smaller patch, or (2) decouple entitlement calculation so it depends only on the invoice event and stops needing subscription-update state — cleaner but touches more code.

**Update (2023-04-08):** Morgan fixed the exponential backoff logic and the retries stopped pileup-ing. Treated as a clean, standalone win, not connected to other ongoing drama.

**Why:** Explains the underlying mechanism behind the customer-facing retry complaints in [[project-billing-webhook-retries-request]] — this was the same root cause driving those asks.
**How to apply:** This issue is resolved as of 2023-04-08. If webhook retry behavior regresses or the customer asks in [[project-billing-webhook-retries-request]] resurface, start from the backoff-timing fix rather than re-diagnosing the race condition from scratch.

source_freshness_warning means the evidence source predates the owner action. It surfaces as a caveat on the record, not an automatic rejection.

Rejection is reserved only for cases where the source or date is too thin to support the action at all — not merely stale relative to the action.

**Why:** Distinguishes "old but still valid evidence, flag it" from "insufficient evidence, block it," so freshness warnings don't get conflated with hard rejections. Ties into [[feedback_compass_prompt_hit_tracking]] (sighting ≠ proof) and the broader Compass hit-tracking discipline.

**How to apply:** When implementing or reviewing Compass evidence validation, treat source_freshness_warning as a non-blocking annotation. Only reject when the source/date genuinely can't support the claimed owner action, regardless of freshness.

Leo Park ran his first Mercury release-risk readout on 2023-07-14 (attendees: Morgan, Leo, Jake, Priya, Marcus). Scope was release risk + evidence only, not a platform roadmap or launch ledger.

**Risk areas identified:**

1. **Org-invite roles vs activation-state seam** — highest risk. Invited-member branch rendering depends on server role + source state, which don't always settle together; a user can accept an invite and land in an ambiguous in-between state showing the wrong branch/CTA. Evidence: only 2 real dogfood invited-member accounts end to end, one bug-bash needed refresh before UI settled, confidence mostly from happy-path staging. Severity: high, confidence: medium. Next: more real invited-member dogfood across admin-first/invitee-first orderings, verify no pseudo-activated state, confirm sample data stays preview-only, watch CTA on first load post-invite.

2. **Release-readiness evidence gaps are themselves material** — "implemented" vs "proven" gap. Invited-member branch thin (2 accounts), queued-sync retry logs sparse, failed-sync screenshots shallow in depth. Severity: high, confidence: high on the gap itself (lower confidence on how many real bugs underlie it). Next: targeted dogfood pass per branch with saved screenshots/logs, one full queue→retry→recovery trace, separate "unproven" from "actually broken."

3. **Failed-sync cleanup unverified end to end** — likely close but not confirmed clean across every normalized bucket (auth/permissions, source unavailable/timeout, unknown/retry). One screenshot still leaked a raw vendor string. Severity: medium, confidence: medium. Next: retest each bucket with captured UI, confirm no raw vendor strings leak, confirm retry stays idempotent.

4. **Explicitly deferred to polish, not blockers** (unless they cause wrong actions/confusion): setup-guide copy, small-width spacing, failed-state icon detail. Jake flagged risk of a polish list becoming a second scope track before the next Mercury cycle.

**Explicit exclusions:** no abstract platform recommendations, no reopening the provider/auth-rewrite debate, no SSO/admin-depth wishlist, not an owner-split launch ledger.

**Open questions for next pass:** can invited-member rendering be proven across real role/source-state permutations (not just happy path)? Is queued-sync retry evidence enough to call recovery understandable? Is failed-sync normalization actually complete or just clean on the common path? Which gaps are real blockers vs thin proof on otherwise-correct behavior? What's the smallest next dogfood pass that meaningfully raises confidence before widening exposure?

**Why:** first readout from [[project_leo_park_onboarding]] in his Mercury ramp; sets the pattern for how his release-risk readouts should be scoped going forward — risk/evidence, not roadmap or ownership assignment.
**How to apply:** when referencing this readout externally (Discord, Friday wrap, etc.), keep the framing as release-risk/evidence, not a launch ledger with owners — that boundary was explicit in the room and matters for how Leo's early work is perceived.

On 2023-03-15, a small (~10 line) change to auth/entitlement logic caused a live outage. Root cause: requests on the new path that hit a cache miss fell through to the old entitlement check, which retried against the worker pool and piled up. Only some tenants hit the bad branch, but each bad request fanned out into ~6-8 internal calls, so dashboards looked half-normal for a long time before the severity was visible. Devon worked traces, Priya rolled traffic back via the edge flag; stragglers persisted after rollback because jobs were already queued.

**Why:** Diff size did not reflect blast radius — asymmetric impact (only some tenants) plus fan-out (1 request → many internal calls) masked the true severity in monitoring.

**How to apply:** When Morgan or the team discusses this incident or writes the retro, the key point is diff size is a bad proxy for risk when the change touches branchy auth/entitlement logic with fallback paths. See [[feedback_flag_replay_before_ship]] for the resulting process change.

**Update 2023-03-16 09:30:** Service restored but Morgan not calling it fully clean yet — some residual ugly edges overnight, team deliberately being cautious/restrictive about deploys that day. Hoped-for all-clear was midday 2023-03-16. Don't treat the incident as closed until Morgan confirms it's boring again; avoid suggesting normal deploy cadence resume until then.

**Resolved 2023-03-16 midday:** Fully recovered, 18 hours end-to-end. Morgan isn't planning a big retro/speech about it, but is genuinely positive on the team — called them sharp throughout, even when it got gross. Incident is closed; normal deploy cadence can resume. Retro/process follow-up is still [[feedback_flag_replay_before_ship]].

**Retro planned 2023-03-17:** Morgan wrote up personal notes the evening of 2023-03-16 (18 hours end-to-end confirmed) and flagged the next day's retro will center on deploy discipline: what got merged when, who had prod access, and why the rollback path was fuzzy. So there is a real process retro after all, focused narrowly on deploy/access/rollback hygiene rather than the entitlement-logic root cause itself.

**Retro day 2023-03-17:** Morgan's stated approach going in: take the deploy-process feedback cleanly, no defending, no long speech — just ticket the obvious fixes. Retro at 11am, then working session with Devon right after to convert findings into concrete owners/dates, tightening PR checks and rollback rules if warranted.

**Lingering effect, check-in 2023-04-12:** Nearly a month later Morgan describes still feeling "cooked" / dragging from this outage — despite the clean-retro intention on 2023-03-17, the post-mortem "turned into its own whole thing" rather than being a quick ticket-and-move-on. Morgan expected to be over it by now and isn't. Don't treat this incident as fully behind Morgan emotionally even though the technical/process side closed out; be mindful of this when the outage or post-mortem comes up, and avoid implying they should already be past it.

**Still ruminating, 2023-04-13:** Morgan refers to this incident as "B1" and says the fix itself was only ~10 lines, not a scary diff — the 18h mess came almost entirely from timing (shipped Wednesday 4:50pm, went weird once people were offline, response dragged through Thursday morning) plus a fuzzy rollback path, not from the root cause itself. **Launch bar:** activation without founder handholding; expansion path visible in product (not slides); top admin pain reduced enough that CS calls stop repeating the same 3 complaints; one blocker owner each.

**Activation** — owners Priya (path/copy/screens), Jake (implementation/flag/rollout sequence), Anna (event definitions + success cut). Cuts: no template gallery, no SSO in first-run path, no advanced permissions during activation, no logo/branding in first-run. **Expansion** — owners Jake (overall), Priya (upgrade moments/UI), Anna (usage-threshold sanity/measurement). Blockers: Mercury feature-flag rollout ambiguous (who flips it, merge criteria, rollback note, target date); usage-threshold cut too noisy, need one number the team will use; upgrade copy split between product/admin language and billing language. Cuts: no annual-plan flow, no seat-management overhaul, no contract-specific enterprise branching, no pricing-story work. Expansion path must exist even if monetization details evolve later; if it needs a sales explanation every time, it's not launch-ready.

**Admin pain** — owners Jake (backend/account actions/audit surfaces), Priya (admin home + settings grouping), Anna (tag incoming issues by severity/frequency). Blockers: audit-log launch-mandatory scope unclear; CSV/import failures don't tell admins what broke; permission-model explanation too hand-wavy for security-conscious customers; notification routing rules not explicit. Cuts: no full settings redesign, no granular notification matrix, no admin analytics dashboard, no custom role builder. Fix the repeated pain, not every admin complaint ever raised; post-launch-scale problems get written down and moved on from.

**Cross-cutting:** Jake runs the weekly spine from this, not Morgan; Morgan only pulled in for actual scope calls/unblocks; Devon can pressure-test logic but not turn it into investor copy; every owner comes to weekly with what moved / what slipped / what got cut; customer examples over opinions; launch-blockers list stays short and named. On 2024-04-25, Nadia finished a margin-notes pass on the Evergreen examples pack after Sarah's live-account notes and Devon's commercial/procurement split, working out which examples count as repeatable customer-growth signal for the next internal read.

Three examples under review:
- Source-workspace copy confusion — keep in display-clarity language, not a permissions-risk or broad admin-state story, unless the backend grant is actually wrong. Matches the resolution shape in [[project_evergreen_member_count_display]] and [[project_acme_billing_display_bug]] (display/cache issues, not backend bugs).
- Stale member-count display after cancel — support hygiene only, already resolved as a cache issue per [[project_evergreen_member_count_display]]; only escalate if it starts recurring as a visible cross-account trust problem.

Procurement-specific objections can inform internal caveats but shouldn't dominate a general weekly read.

Nadia's own read: the safest reusable pattern is that admin-state wording changes how buyers interpret current-product truth; the weakest is any example that depends more on one account's procurement vocabulary than on repeated product/admin behavior.

**Why:** Extends the bounded-scope discipline from [[project_evergreen_test_review_roles]] and [[project_nadia_prestart_packet]] into Nadia's own customer-growth reads — keeps Evergreen-specific procurement language from leaking into general internal material, same failure mode tracked across the many occurrences in [[project_evergreen_second_admin_group_asks]].

**How to apply:** When drafting or reviewing the next internal customer-growth read, keep source-workspace and member-count examples framed as display issues (not permissions/trust stories) unless new evidence says otherwise, treat auditability wording as buyer-language sensitivity distinct from actual audit-history status, keep Sarah as the named Evergreen continuity owner, and don't let procurement-specific vocabulary from one account generalize into the broader read.

**How to apply:** If asked to help plan, don't default to suggesting something bigger (all-hands announcement, press, big event) unless Morgan asks — respect the low-key framing. Fine to help with logistics (dinner reservation, guest list) if asked.

As of 2023-01-16, Morgan's hiring question narrowed from an abstract caution to a concrete decision: whether to open reqs now for 2 specific eng hires. Good candidates are on the market now, so Morgan doesn't want to be cute about timing — but is also wary of cramming 2 new people onto a 12-person team, botching onboarding, and having to explain burn in every investor update for the next 6 months if the round drags.

Same-day (2023-01-16), meeting Devon in the afternoon, leaning toward first mapping the exact headcount line: what changes at 14 that doesn't at 12, and what can wait until post-raise.

**Decision (2023-01-30, post Devon call):** Hiring is punted until post-raise. Morgan is explicit this isn't a principled stance, just that the 12-vs-14 capability delta was never answered — adding a req now would create work and story drift without a clear justification. No movement on recruiters or JD drafts for now. The latest headcount pass should be kept handy (not discarded) for when the raise closes.

**Why:** Consistent with [[project-scaffold-trajectory]] — Morgan was already wary of overcorrecting on headcount before a trend was proven out, and the 12-vs-14 mapping never produced a clear answer. This is the resolution of that open question.
**How to apply:** Do not propose or draft recruiter outreach or JDs for these eng reqs unless Morgan reopens this. If asked about hiring plans, headcount, or the deck's team narrative, note hiring is paused until post-raise and that reqs may resume then using the existing headcount pass — don't reintroduce the 12-vs-14 framing as if it's still open.

**Update (2023-02-03):** Morgan had a JD draft in progress and put an explicit hold note on it rather than closing it outright — wording along the lines of "pausing this search until post-raise, will reopen if the headcount line still makes sense at 14." Morgan's stated reason: a stale draft that still looks active is how outdated plans linger and accidentally get acted on later. Treat this as a general pattern, not just a one-off for this JD — when a document or plan is paused rather than cancelled, prefer an explicit "on hold, here's the reopen condition" note over just leaving it untouched or silently dropping it.

**Update (2023-04-05):** Still 12 people at Scaffold's 2-year mark. Morgan frames the steady headcount as a plus, not a stalled hiring plan — easier to hold the company in his head, and credits it in part for how the [[project-next-90-days-reset]] pullback has held up.

**Update (2023-04-14):** When hiring does resume, Morgan is leaning toward sequencing a senior eng hire before any go-to-market hire, tied to [[project-mercury-q3-release]] still being pre-v0.1. Reasoning: not a principled stance, just doesn't want to hire someone into a story that's still changing every 3 days — better to wait until there's a real v0.1 in customers' hands before layering in GTM.

**Update (2023-04-16):** Hiring has actually moved forward for the senior eng role — an offer is drafted (185k base, 0.15% equity) and just waiting on legal to clear it before recruiting can send. Only blocker is legal sitting on it.

**Update (2023-04-19):** A separate staff eng search is also underway via a recruiter. First screening call felt genuinely good to Morgan (rare, per Morgan — usually hard to read signal from recruiter calls), and one candidate is being moved to onsite next week. Morgan is deliberately holding back from reading too much into a single call.

**Update (2023-04-27):** New disagreement with Jake surfaced, specifically about how to staff [[project_mercury_q3_release]]. Jake is dug in on two senior eng hires before any mid-level, arguing leverage over ramp — strong seniors can absorb ambiguity and cut rework. Morgan's counter is time-to-productive: at 12 people with Mercury already well-scoped, a mid-level who ramps in weeks is more "real" than a 3-month hold-out for a Staff-level profile at ~$230k plus recruiter fees. Morgan is leaning one senior + one mid if sequencing works, and is wary of making the hiring plan hostage to a search market Morgan sees as bad right now.
**Why:** Extends the 2023-04-14 sequencing lean (senior-first, tied to Mercury timing) into an actual composition dispute now that a senior offer is out and staff search is live — this is Morgan pushing back on Jake's preferred shape, not a settled decision.
**How to apply:** Don't assume "two seniors" is the plan — as of 2023-04-27 this is unresolved and Morgan favors 1 senior + 1 mid. If asked to help with JDs, sourcing, or hiring plan framing, reflect this as an open disagreement with Jake rather than picking a side.

**Update (2023-06-22):** Leo Park signed the staff eng offer (from the 2023-04-19 search); July 10 start confirmed. Decision, per Devon and accepted by Morgan: Leo is the July 10 senior technical anchor for Mercury release discipline, platform seams, and launch readiness. The second Mercury engineering hire is explicitly delayed, not cancelled — revisit is tied to July launch-readiness feedback after Leo lands, not to reopening the old two-senior plan. Jake pushed back (still wants two seniors in parallel, citing leverage for release discipline + platform cleanup) but was not asking to open a second req blindly today — Devon and Morgan held the delay.
**Why:** Leo's signing is the concrete headcount decision point the 2023-04-27 senior/senior vs senior/mid disagreement was waiting on. Devon and Morgan explicitly rejected "resurrect the old two-senior plan by default" reasoning — the next req should be justified by July signals, not by matching a prior plan.
**How to apply:** Don't treat Leo's hire as satisfying or reopening the two-senior plan either way. If asked about the second Mercury eng slot before July launch-readiness feedback is in, say it's deliberately on hold pending that feedback — don't draft JDs/reqs for it, and don't frame it as settled in either direction (not "two seniors after all," not "no more senior hires").

**Update (2023-07-27, Mercury eng headcount checkpoint w/ Devon + Jake):** Decision made. Do not reopen the second Mercury eng req now, and no more arbitrary month-end revisit dates — the old "revisit after July" placeholder is replaced by an evidence trigger. Candidate pipeline can stay cold until then. Jake still pushed to reopen now (wants senior depth, worried about launch-critical ambiguity resting on too few people — Marcus/Leo/Jake absorbing everything while Priya still holds activation UX decisions), but Devon held that the pipeline doesn't support a reflex reopen (would be a fresh search, not converting an active one), and Morgan agreed a decision rule tied to product-readiness evidence should replace the calendar-based habit. Morgan's framing: July's real signal is that Leo ([[project_leo_mercury_release_risk_readout_20230714]]) is finding the right seams, and [[project_mer1279_launch_readiness_ledger]] now centralizes that risk instead of it being scattered across PRs/Figma/Discord — keep this as launch-readiness operating logic, not an investor story.

Next look is triggered only by external launch-readiness feedback from design-partner conversations/trials — specifically: source setup failure cases seen by external users, admin/invited-member handoff clarity, time-to-first-sync comfort/trust, which failure states are understandable vs confusing, and whether remaining blockers look like depth problems or execution-throughput problems.

Decision rule for the next req, once that evidence is in:
1. Senior-engineer req if external feedback shows repeated platform/architecture-seam failures needing independent senior ownership.
2. Mid-level implementer req if the core user path is understandable but the limiting factor is cleanup throughput, follow-through, and launch hardening.
3. No immediate req if external users can get through setup, admin handoff, early sync, and failure recovery with manageable issues the current owner split (Marcus: implementation gates/dogfood blockers; Priya: design/Figma source of truth; Leo: cross-service platform-seam risk notes; Jake: uses the ledger in the Mercury weekly) can close from the ledger.

**Why:** Resolves the 2023-06-22 "revisit tied to July launch-readiness feedback" open question with an actual evidence-based trigger instead of a date, and settles (for now) the standing senior-vs-mid/Jake-vs-Devon-Morgan tension from 2023-04-27 and 2023-06-22.
**How to apply:** If asked about the second Mercury eng slot, say it's on hold with no set revisit date — the trigger is external design-partner/trial feedback on setup, admin handoff, first-sync trust, and failure-state legibility. Don't draft JDs/reqs preemptively. When that feedback arrives, apply the three-way decision rule above rather than defaulting to "senior" or re-litigating headcount shape from scratch.

**Update (2024-01-08):** The 2023 senior-engineer offer (the one stuck on legal per 2023-04-16) is now formally closed — no signed offer/paperwork ever came back, HR closed the candidate record as no-hire, archived the November packet, and disabled the signature link. Morgan had HR confirm this explicitly in writing before treating any January artifact as inactive.
**Why:** Closes the loop on the 2023-04-16 "waiting on legal" update, which never resolved — the offer lapsed rather than being signed.
**How to apply:** Don't reference a live/pending senior-engineer offer or packet from this process going forward. Any future senior or principal eng hire (including a revived second-Mercury-eng-slot decision under the rule above) requires a fresh req and current legal/recruiting checks — it can't be reactivated from the November packet.

**Update (2024-02-26, post-close leadership reset — see [[project_post_close_leadership_reset_feb2024]]):** Decision made, unambiguous: the second Mercury engineering req stays closed/not reopened — the evidence-trigger rule from 2023-07-27 is not being invoked right now. Instead, the first new search to scope post-close is a customer-growth/GTM leader, not Mercury engineering. Devon + HR draft the role description; Morgan reviews before it goes wider than the small reset group. Role intent: build a repeatable customer-growth motion out of Mercury/Evergreen-like pull without turning accounts into bespoke commitments or product-roadmap negotiating sessions.
**Why:** Resolves any ambiguity coming out of the Series B close about whether closing triggers a hiring wave — it doesn't. The reset explicitly separated "more room" from "bigger story," and hiring sequencing followed that line.
**How to apply:** If asked about hiring plans post-close, state plainly: no second Mercury eng req reopened, first search in flight is customer-growth/GTM (Devon+HR drafting, Morgan reviewing). Don't imply Mercury eng hiring is the next move, and don't draft Mercury eng JDs/reqs off the close.

**Update (2024-04-05):** HR confirmed a corrected senior-engineer offer file matches current terms and can stay in its existing routing path — no changes needed. Candidate-facing movement (e.g., sending the offer) was pushed out past this day regardless.
**Why:** This is a distinct, separate senior-engineer hiring thread from the 2023 offer closed 2024-01-08 — not enough context yet to tell if it's tied to the evidence-trigger rule from 2023-07-27 or a different req entirely.
**How to apply:** Don't conflate this with the closed 2023 offer or assume it reopens the second Mercury eng slot. If asked about this offer's status, say HR cleared the corrected file for its current routing path as of 2024-04-05, but nothing was sent to the candidate that day; get more context before characterizing which req this belongs to.

**Update (2024-06-14):** Decision, per Morgan + Devon: do not open RevOps, CS, SDR, or field-sales lanes in Q3. This follows Nadia's 60-day read on the customer-growth cadence (the GTM-leader search opened 2024-02-26) — the cadence is clearly useful but still too manual, and what's needed next is more reliable account-note inputs and cleaner source material, not a junior team for Nadia to manage. HR is asked to keep the customer-growth org shape quiet for now (i.e., don't circulate any org chart/headcount plan for these lanes). Revisit is tied to two more cadence cycles plus the July Evergreen review producing better evidence — not a calendar date.
**Why:** Extends the 2024-02-26 GTM-leader search outcome — Nadia is now hired and operating, and this is the first headcount-shape decision since she started, made on read-quality evidence rather than a default "hire a team under the new leader" assumption.
**How to apply:** If asked about customer-growth/GTM headcount, org shape, or opening RevOps/CS/SDR/field-sales reqs, say these are explicitly not opening in Q3 pending better account-note inputs and Nadia's next two cadence cycles + the July Evergreen review. Don't draft JDs/org charts for these lanes, and don't circulate the org shape outside the small group until Morgan/Devon lift the quiet-hold.

**Update (2024-06-24, Q2 board update):** Morgan told the board directly, not just internally: no broad leadership search, no field-sales build, no RevOps/CS lane, and no second Mercury eng req in Q3. Board framing was explicit and tradeoff-forward: Nadia's customer-growth cadence works but isn't team-scale evidence yet; Leo's release-risk reviews are improving Mercury discipline; Rishi's departure for Tessl (see [[project_rishi_tessl_intro_thought]]) left a real Atlas gap that the interim split (Leo/Jake, see [[project_rishi_atlas_ownership]]) can manage but not erase. Morgan was explicit to the board that hiring after Q3 still needs evidence (Nadia's cadence, Evergreen's July review, Mercury release discipline, Atlas transition stability) as the trigger — not the Series B close itself.
**Why:** This is the same 2024-06-14 internal freeze now stated to the board, plus an explicit rejection of "Series B closed, therefore hire" reasoning — Morgan is drawing a hard line between funding and headcount triggers.
**How to apply:** If asked whether the Series B close changes hiring plans, say no — the close is not a hiring trigger; evidence from Nadia/Evergreen/Mercury/Atlas is. This board framing is consistent with, not a change from, the 2024-06-14 decision.

**Update (2024-07-18):** Morgan sent HR a note reaffirming the 2024-06-14 freeze: Nadia's first-90 read landed well but does not change the Q3 hiring plan. Still no RevOps, CS, SDR, field-sales, or adjacent junior GTM lanes in Q3. Nadia is confirmed as owner of the lightweight weekly customer-growth cadence coming out of onboarding — the cadence itself is producing clearer signal (activation friction, admin handoff confusion, procurement/security packaging, post-first-sync expansion stalls) when Sarah's thread notes and Devon's procurement context are clean, but inputs are still too hand-built/uneven to justify adding headcount. Useful interim work named: account-note hygiene, routing enterprise-readiness requests through the right owner, and a Q4 team-shape revisit gated on the signal becoming repeatable from Evergreen-style conversations (not a calendar date).
**Why:** This is the first explicit checkpoint since Nadia started (per 2024-06-14) — confirms the freeze held rather than loosening once she had a track record, and names Q4 + Evergreen-repeatability as the actual gate.
**How to apply:** If asked about Q3/Q4 GTM headcount, say the freeze held as of 2024-07-18 and the gate is signal-repeatability from Evergreen-style conversations, not a date. Nadia owns the weekly cadence; don't propose junior GTM hires or org shape until that gate is discussed.

**Update (2024-09-25):** Morgan and Devon extended the freeze into Q4, explicitly post-Series-B. Trigger this time: Nadia's first stronger enterprise-readiness plan pulled too far toward bespoke, one-account asks, and enterprise-readiness work was starting to drag roadmap gravity toward larger customers (see [[project_nadia_roadmap_commitment_boundary]]). Decision: Q4 still has no broad field-sales build, no RevOps/CS lane, and no second Mercury eng req — gate remains adoption + renewal/expansion signal + account-source quality repeating, not the Series B raise itself. Morgan frames this as a good outcome: deliberate enterprise follow-through rather than post-close hiring acceleration, and real board cover for saying no when a single-account conversation tries to become roadmap.
**Why:** Confirms the 2024-06-24 board line ("close is not a hiring trigger") held through Q4 planning and ties the freeze explicitly to Nadia's bespoke-ask overreach rather than a calendar checkpoint.
**How to apply:** If asked about Q4 hiring/GTM headcount post-Series-B, say the freeze holds — no field-sales, no RevOps/CS, no second Mercury eng req — until adoption, renewal/expansion signal, and account-source quality repeat. Frame any one-account enterprise ask (Evergreen-style) as evidence to route through the existing owner map, not as grounds to open headcount.

**Update (2024-12-06):** Q1 2025 planning question from HR: does Evergreen's paid pilot ([[project_evergreen_paid_pilot_signed]]) plus Nadia's cleaner account conversations justify opening RevOps, CS, SDR, field-sales, or the second Mercury eng req early in 2025? Morgan and Devon's answer: no Q1 openings for any of those lanes. Staying lightweight — Nadia keeps her individual weekly read, Sarah continues account-note input hygiene, nothing scales up yet. Team-shape gets revisited only after the January Evergreen renewal/pilot evidence lands, alongside materially repeatable (not one-off) account-source quality, owner-routed enterprise-readiness intake, and shipped enterprise-readiness adoption. Morgan also reaffirmed the Mercury roadmap boundary from [[project_nadia_roadmap_commitment_boundary]]: one enterprise account's conversations still aren't enough to justify bespoke roadmap commitments.
**Why:** First Q1-2025-specific checkpoint since the 2024-09-25 Q4 freeze — confirms the same evidence-gated approach carries forward into next year's planning cycle rather than resetting with the new year or the Evergreen pilot's initial success.
**How to apply:** If asked about Q1 2025 hiring/GTM headcount, say there are no openings planned for RevOps, CS, SDR, field-sales, or the second Mercury eng req — the gate is the January Evergreen renewal/pilot evidence plus repeatable (not single-account) source quality and shipped enterprise-readiness adoption. Don't treat Evergreen's pilot signing or Nadia's improved conversations alone as sufficient to open these lanes, and keep the Mercury roadmap boundary intact when Evergreen-style asks come up.

Morgan and Devon's answer: no — don't open a req off Evergreen alone. Nadia's weekly customer-growth cadence plus Sarah's account-thread hygiene remain the operating model; a single account's live thread isn't the repeatable-signal evidence the 2024-12-06 gate calls for. Revisit only if the January Mercury and Evergreen evidence turns into repeatable proof across accounts, not off this one thread.
**Why:** Same evidence-gate logic as 2024-12-06 and the Nadia bespoke-ask boundary — Morgan is again drawing the line at "one account's momentum isn't team-scale evidence," this time specifically pushing back on HR's default-to-recruiting-lane framing.
**How to apply:** If HR or Devon raise the Evergreen thread as a hiring trigger, say plainly: not opening a req off this alone; Nadia+Sarah's existing cadence/hygiene stays the model until January's evidence repeats across accounts, not just this one.

**Update (2025-03-14):** Post-board Q1 operating read with Sofia formalized into an HR-facing record — see [[project_customer_growth_staffing_plan_2025_spring]] (plan_id customer_growth_staffing_plan_2025_spring). No hires planned; gate is the May 2025 board-cycle review producing Compass behavior-change evidence, repeatable account-source quality beyond Evergreen Bank, and owner-routed enterprise-readiness intake.

**Update (2025-12-12):** Dec 12 Q4 operating review did not reopen the second Mercury engineering req; keep the req closed from this review.

**Update (2026-04-17):** The senior customer-growth candidate who'd been sent a clear hold note (Head of Customer Growth backfill, not reopened per board review) replied warmly — understands the backfill stays closed, offered to stay in touch if evidence changes, and offered a retention-playbook note. Morgan is not taking the playbook and does not want HR reopening a process off this reply.

As of 2023-01-18, Morgan batched the first round of Series B investor intros instead of sending them out one at a time as they came up. A few of these are just temperature-check calls rather than serious pitches, which Morgan considers fine/expected at this stage.

**Why:** Morgan felt the previous one-off approach was messier; batching is described as "cleaner." This decision came the same day the [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]] spine was resolved with Devon, suggesting Morgan is now moving from internal alignment into external execution on the raise.
**How to apply:** When helping with investor outreach, scheduling, or follow-ups for the Series B, assume intros are going out in batches rather than ad hoc, and that not every call is a full pitch — some are early temperature checks and shouldn't be treated as urgent/high-stakes by default.

Later the same day (2023-01-18, 17:00), Morgan drafted and sent a follow-up to two of the firms from that first batch, kept deliberately tight: one update, one ask, no extra preamble. See [[feedback_concise_investor_comms]] for the general style preference this reflects.

On 2023-01-19, Devon sent Morgan a list of ~15 additional investor names. Morgan triaged the full list into maybe/probably/skip buckets and pushed notes back on each. Most skips are because a firm is too late-stage or would expect a cleaner growth story than Scaffold currently has (see [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]] tension over growth framing). Only 3 names from this batch were judged actually worth spending time on.

**Why:** Same rationale as the batching decision — Morgan is filtering aggressively rather than chasing every lead, prioritizing fit (especially around the growth-story concern) over volume.
**How to apply:** When helping with outreach or follow-up planning from Devon's list, treat it as a small, already-filtered shortlist (~3 names) rather than the full 15 — the rest were deliberately screened out, not just deprioritized.

As of 2023-02-03, ~8 intro calls are booked for early February, mostly with the firms Morgan wanted, and the lead-firm meeting is locked for week 2 of February. Morgan is treating these first calls explicitly as filtering, not just pitching, on the belief that partner-level chemistry matters more at this stage than most people admit.

**How to apply:** When helping prep for these calls, frame them as two-way evaluation (assessing partner fit) rather than pure pitch prep — e.g. materials or talking points should help Morgan read the room, not just sell.

On 2023-02-05 (Sunday), Morgan prepped for a heavy week ahead: five investor meetings across four days. Plan is a deck pass Sunday night, then rehearsing just the first 2-3 walk-in lines until they sound natural rather than over-polished. Morgan is deliberately pacing rather than over-preparing, wants clean openings and enough space between calls to avoid burning out by Wednesday, and is relying on Devon to own the data room so Morgan can focus on the room itself.

**Why:** With ~8 calls compressed into early February (see above) and a lead-firm meeting in the mix, Morgan is managing energy/pacing as much as content — the risk framed as "improvising dumbly" rather than being unprepared.
**How to apply:** When helping with prep this week, favor lightweight/targeted help (tightening an opening line, sanity-checking pacing/scheduling gaps) over generating extensive new materials; don't assume Morgan wants full pitch rehearsal for every call, and route data-room questions to Devon rather than Morgan.

On 2023-02-06, Morgan gave the first B-round pitch and it went well — described the room as "with her the whole time." Debriefed with Devon right after; both read it as a strong, likely-to-land meeting, though Morgan is consciously not getting ahead of it before anything is finalized.

**Why:** This is the first data point from the ~8-call batch described above, and it's a good one — worth tracking as a signal that the deck/pacing approach from the 2023-02-05 prep is working.
**How to apply:** Treat this as early positive momentum, not a done deal — Morgan is deliberately guarded about calling it before it closes. Don't assume the round is closing based on this alone; four more meetings remain this week per the 2023-02-05 plan.

On 2023-02-07, Morgan had two calls booked. The first went fine, nothing notable, deck held up well. Morgan did a quick numbers-slide pass before the second.

**Why:** Another routine, unremarkable data point in the ongoing call sequence — consistent with the momentum from 2023-02-06 rather than a new signal.
**How to apply:** No action needed; continues to support treating the deck/pacing as solid. Keep tracking for any call that breaks this pattern (either a strong win worth flagging or friction worth noting).

On 2023-02-09, Morgan had two more calls, both strong. Explicitly said "not doing the victory lap thing" but told Devon afterward "we're close, this one's gonna land."

**Why:** This is a notable shift from the earlier guarded stance (2023-02-06/07) — Morgan is still resisting overconfidence in words but the substance of what was said to Devon ("we're close") is more bullish than prior debriefs. Four strong/fine calls in a row now with no friction reported.
**How to apply:** Reflect growing (if self-consciously restrained) confidence in the round closing, but keep mirroring Morgan's own framing — don't call it done or treat it as closed until Morgan does. Still watch for the first call that breaks the streak.

On 2023-02-10, the last day of week 1 of meetings, Morgan has 2 more investor meetings followed by a debrief with Devon. Plan for the day is coffee and skipping lunch, same pattern as before, to just get through the day. Same day, Morgan explicitly froze the [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]] — no more edits unless something is actually broken.

**Why:** End of a demanding first week (five+ meetings); Morgan is managing energy by keeping the day minimal rather than adding prep or polish on top of it.
**How to apply:** Don't suggest deck changes or extra prep work for this stretch — support Morgan getting through the day, not optimizing it further.

Later on 2023-02-10, Morgan debriefed the day's second meeting: "fine, not our best room and they were a little hard to read, but nothing broke." Follow-up (deck, metrics snapshot, and the one customer note the investor asked for) was already sent same-day.

**Why:** This is the first call in the batch that breaks the four-in-a-row strong streak from 2023-02-06 through 2023-02-09 — not a bad call, but a flatter, harder-to-read room. Worth tracking as the first data point that isn't uniformly positive.
**How to apply:** Don't treat this as a red flag or a lost deal — Morgan's own framing is neutral ("nothing broke"). But stop assuming every remaining call will mirror the strong streak; watch for whether this room follows up or goes quiet, which would be a better signal than the debrief itself.

As of 2023-02-15, the lead firm has gone quiet since Monday's partner meeting (2023-02-13, see [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]]) — no follow-up, no diligence pings. Morgan is anxious about the silence but trying not to over-read it; the data room is clean and ready on Scaffold's side (Devon), so there's nothing outstanding to push on.
**Why:** After a meeting that "felt fine" but exposed a real retention data gap, silence is ambiguous — could be normal diligence pacing/internal deliberation, or could signal cooling interest. Morgan's own framing is explicitly resisting catastrophizing.
**How to apply:** Don't suggest proactive check-ins or follow-up nudges to the lead firm unless Morgan raises it — the data room is ready, so there's no actionable next step on Scaffold's side right now. If asked, help Morgan calibrate what "quiet" typically means in diligence timelines rather than reinforcing worst-case reads.

On 2023-02-17, the lead firm passed. This lands the day after the silence noted on 2023-02-15 and follows the retention data-gap exposed at the 2023-02-13 partner meeting (see [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]]). Morgan cleared the afternoon of 2023-02-17 to recover rather than stacking more meetings on top of the news; see [[feedback_post_bad_news_scheduling]] for the resulting scheduling pattern.

**Why:** The lead-firm meeting was the centerpiece of the ~8-call batch and the meeting where the retention/cohort data question first surfaced unresolved — this is the round's most consequential setback so far, not a routine "quiet" data point.
**How to apply:** Don't treat this as just another call outcome in the sequence — it changes the state of the round (lead firm gone) and should shape any advice on next steps, remaining calls, or how to talk about the round's status. Don't assume the round is dead either; wait for Morgan's read on what comes next (e.g., re-approaching another firm as lead) before speculating.

On 2023-02-19, two days after the lead passed, Morgan checked in: "not back to 100. but moving." Started mapping the next two weeks as concrete days instead of a vague blob — a couple of cleanup conversations being avoided, internal work with Devon, and re-integrating the team back to normal work without making it feel forced or heavy.

**Why:** First sign of Morgan moving from acute post-bad-news recovery (see [[feedback_post_bad_news_scheduling]]) into forward planning, but explicitly not fully recovered yet.
**How to apply:** Treat this as early-stage recovery, not a full return to normal — don't ramp scheduling or workload back up to pre-news levels yet. If Morgan raises the team-normalization question or the Devon internal convos, help think through pacing/tone rather than pushing solutions; Morgan is still feeling this out.

On 2023-02-20, Elena Volkov (a VC at one of the firms from this batch) passed — a long, non-boilerplate note that Morgan read twice. Her main objection was the retention funnel: she didn't buy that Scaffold has earned the shape it's implying there yet. Morgan finds this annoying but fair, and is keeping Elena in a "later" bucket rather than writing her off.

**Why:** This is an independent, external confirmation of the exact retention/cohort weak spot the lead partner also flagged on 2023-02-13 (see [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]]) — not a new problem, but a second data point that the concern is real and visible to sophisticated investors, not a one-off nitpick.
**How to apply:** Don't treat this as a routine pass in the sequence — it reinforces that the retention story needs to actually be fixed (per the ongoing cohort-cut work in [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]]), not just better-explained in the room. If Morgan mentions re-approaching Elena Volkov later, treat her as a warm, thoughtful re-engage candidate once the retention data is stronger — not a cold outreach.

On 2023-02-21, after two more soft/inconclusive investor conversations, Morgan decided the round is deferred: "we're not raising this month." Said out loud to Devon on a walk, described as not a big dramatic thing, just an acknowledgment of where things stand. Morgan noted the day felt "weirdly empty" afterward.

**Why:** This is the resolution of the arc that started with the lead firm's silence (2023-02-15), the lead passing (2023-02-17), and Elena Volkov's pass reinforcing the same retention concern (2023-02-20) — the round didn't fail dramatically, it just didn't gather enough momentum to close this cycle, so Morgan is calling it rather than letting it drag.
**How to apply:** Treat the Series B as paused/deferred, not dead and not "closing soon" — don't suggest scheduling more investor calls or pushing the deck/data room forward unless Morgan reopens it. If asked about next steps, follow Morgan's lead on timeline (e.g., revisiting once the retention story is stronger, per [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]]) rather than assuming urgency. This is likely a moment for a lighter schedule, similar to [[feedback_post_bad_news_scheduling]], even though Morgan is framing it calmly rather than as an acute setback.

On 2023-02-22, Morgan settled the shape of the board note about the deferred round: stop framing Q2 as the story, be direct that this round's market/terms weren't there, existing investors are willing to bridge, and Q3 launch becomes the milestone people can actually underwrite. Spend posture tightens now — tighter hiring, eng stays on launch-critical path only, no speculative GTM experiments. Devon will own the cash/runway math section since he has the less hand-wavy version of those numbers. Morgan wants the note to read as a decision, not fallout.

**Why:** This is the direct next step after calling the round deferred on 2023-02-21 — Morgan moved quickly from "we're not raising this month" into a concrete plan (bridge + Q3 launch + spend discipline) rather than sitting in ambiguity, and wants the board to hear a controlled decision rather than damage control.
**How to apply:** If asked to help draft or review the board note, keep the framing direct and decision-oriented (not apologetic or hedging), lead with the bridge/Q3-launch narrative rather than lingering on Q2, and route cash/runway specifics to Devon's section rather than inventing numbers. Also relevant to [[project-scaffold-hiring-scope]] since the tighter-hiring posture reinforces that prior decision rather than reopening it.

On 2023-03-04, Morgan put a low-key mid-March coffee with Elena Volkov on the calendar (30 min, Blue Bottle on Sansome). Morgan is explicit about not reading too much into it — just keeping the relationship warm — because Elena "thinks carefully" and Morgan wants her in the mix if the round comes back around later.

**Why:** Direct follow-through on the "later bucket" plan from 2023-02-20 — Elena's pass was thoughtful and tied to the same retention concern the round overall stalled on, so Morgan is treating her as a relationship to maintain rather than a closed door.
**How to apply:** Treat this as low-stakes relationship maintenance, not a pitch or re-raise signal — don't suggest prep materials or treat it as reopening the round. If Morgan mentions Elena again, frame her as a warm, deliberately-nurtured contact for a future raise, not a live lead.

On 2023-04-16, an investor meeting (unspecified firm) went well. Morgan now owes a follow-up deck by end of month (2023-04-30), with an explicit ask from the investor for the growth numbers to be "really clean." Morgan's reaction was mixed — glad the meeting landed, but immediately felt scattered ("6 other tabs open") just adding it to the list.

**Why:** This surfaces after the B-round was pushed to H2 2023-03-08 (see [[project-devon-prior-month-conversation]]) — suggests some live investor engagement is continuing even though the formal raise timeline is H2. The "clean growth numbers" ask directly intersects the unresolved growth-vs-retention framing tension in [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]] (Devon wanted growth-forward; Morgan resisted vanity/top-of-funnel framing).
**How to apply:** If asked to help with this follow-up deck, treat the end-of-month (2023-04-30) deadline as real and apply the same growth-framing discipline from [[project-scaffold-seriesb-deck]] — net new ARR + expansion, not pipeline/logo count, even though this investor explicitly asked for growth numbers. Don't assume this reopens the full B-round process; it reads as a single relationship/follow-up, not a new batch of intros.
